title: Empty legs: how one-way private jet availability works
description: Why empty legs exist, what to check before booking one, and what a broker must tell you about the operator, explained from the official rules on charter.
lead: An empty leg is a flight an aircraft has to make anyway, without passengers, to reach its next trip or return home. Here is how they work, and what to check before you book one.

p: Private jets are chartered as a whole aircraft: {{empty.single_entity}}. When a client books a one-way trip, the aircraft often has to fly back to its base, or on to where its next client is waiting. That positioning flight is the empty leg.

Positioning is part of how operators plan their work: {{empty.positioning_counts}}. That is one reason empty legs can change at short notice: the operator plans them around the paying trips, crew rest and maintenance, not around the empty leg.

sections.h: What makes an empty leg a good fit
p: An empty leg suits travellers who can be flexible. The date, the time and sometimes the airport follow the main trip, and if that trip moves or is cancelled, the empty leg can move or disappear with it. If your plans are fixed, a normal charter is usually the safer choice; if they are flexible, an empty leg can be a good match.
The operator, the aircraft, the crew and the safety checks are exactly the same as on any other charter flight. We check them in the same way before we offer the flight to you.

sections.h: What a broker must tell you
p: The United States has written rules for charter brokers, and they are a good standard anywhere. {{empty.us_broker_definition}}. {{empty.ads_say_broker}}, and {{empty.licensed_carrier}}.
We follow the same principle on every booking, wherever it flies: the operator in control of your flight is named in your quote and in your charter agreement before you confirm.

sections.h: How to book one through us
p: Tell us where you would like to go and how flexible you are. We look for aircraft already positioning in your direction and confirm the details with the operator. Any aircraft, any route, upon availability.

faq.q: Can an empty leg be cancelled?
faq.a: Yes. An empty leg depends on the main trip it is attached to. If that trip changes, the operator may change or cancel the empty leg. We explain the operator's terms for that case before you confirm.

faq.q: Is an empty leg flight less safe?
faq.a: No. It is flown by the same licensed operator, aircraft and crew as any charter. We check the operator in the same way.
